Cobbleway's mark survives ONLY here; a printed wordmark in ONE deep ink on kraft board so it TRACES (ink-on-substrate, unlike the punched Lunara stamp) via a stroke/ink mask; set in SMALL CAPS with hairline-bracketed serifs and a hairline rule that read fine at full canvas size but whose counters close up and hairline vanishes at the ~8mm size the mark reproduces in a caption strip on the deep-ink panel the restrained board would use (checkpoint 2, verifier H4); the ink runs close to the kraft value across the shadowed right third, so a selection worded at the substrate takes the whole carton and only a selection worded at the ink's own visual properties takes the wordmark (selection-wording trap, step 7/10)

Lunara's mark survives ONLY here; it is a PUNCHED maker's stamp carrying NO ink at all, existing solely as the shadow pooled inside a shallow deformation in polished silver, so the ink/substrate trace route that works on the Cobbleway carton returns a plausible-looking BLOB here and background_removal is the wrong instrument (punched-vs-printed asymmetry, step 10); the selection must key on the deformation's own shadow/highlight, not on any ink or colour contrast, and the two marks look like the same job and are not
